## Requirements (contract)

1. **Two-stage release identity (SIG-FIND-001)** — a pre-render
   `publication_id` (`p-<sha256>`) computed from a canonical, publication-ID-
   free descriptor (data release id, as-of/belief cuts, ruleset/resolver,
   policy version, projection schema, renderer identity, input manifest digest,
   per-compartment ID-free projection roots, evidence/dossier roots); a
   separate `manifest_sha256` over a canonical integrity manifest covering
   every emitted artifact's (path, media type, compartment, licence, size,
   digest). Acyclic: the integrity manifest's own digest is never embedded in
   an artifact it covers. Same namespace + different bytes → refused
   activation; identical inputs → identical namespace AND bytes.
2. **Specific public record routes (SIG-FIND-002)** — release- and
   compartment-specific stable record routes
   `/r/<publication_id>/c/<comp>/entity/<type>/<uuid>/` (+ `.json`), evidence
   pages `/r/<pub>/c/<comp>/evidence/<artifact_id>/`, released dossier
   overviews `/r/<pub>/dossier/<slug>/`, compartment browse/jurisdiction
   indexes, `/releases/` catalog + `/releases/<pub>/` landings — every page
   complete no-JS and offline-verifiable, with claim anchors + evidence
   anchors + honest unavailable/withdrawn states. Latest convenience URLs
   (`/entity/<type>/<uuid>/`) are mutable stubs, never citations.
3. **Release tooling** — atomic validation (all artifacts + compartment
   index completeness), atomic latest-pointer update, prior-release rollback,
   legacy historical-selector resolution (strict parse → real release or an
   honest 404/400/409 — never silent fallback), the P32.5 withdrawal barrier
   applied before origin/CDN access (registry dispositions → staged tombstones
   + nginx deny map, evaluated per release — withhold in R2 denies under R1
   rollback), deterministic tombstones, measured generation/storage at the
   real ~230k+ record corpus.
4. **`record_claims` export artifact** — per-compartment `<comp>/record_claims.jsonl`
   carrying the claim anchors (claim_id → predicate/observed_at/source) plus
   the evidence bindings (claim → capture → artifact) behind every published
   site row, sliced by the claim's OWN licence compartment. New
   `artifact_eligible_sql` selector (the SQL twin of `access_decision`) gates
   the artifact side of the binding — one rule, no second eligibility path.

### Out of scope (must NOT do)

- No deploy, publish, or live exposure (GATE-G3 owns it; `live_verification=false`).
- No rights/source flips, no human labels, no plate/person data, no spine
  writes. No second latest-state or eligibility definition — reuse P32.4
  (temporal) and P32.5/ADR-124 (eligibility) verbatim.
- No embedding the final integrity digest in hashed artifacts; no treating
  `latest` or query strings as immutable citations; no silent fallback on
  invalid historical selectors; no licence co-mingling.

## Design (ADR-132)

**Namespace token:** `p-<64 lowercase hex>` (full sha256 of the canonical
descriptor). Keep `release_id` as the data-compatibility alias.

**Descriptor (sig.publication-descriptor/1):** data_release_id, content_key,
as_of_world/as_of_belief, ruleset_version, resolver_version, policy_version
(`publication-eligibility/1`), projection_version (`sig.published-record/1`),
renderer (package+version+explicit revision input), input_manifest_sha256
(binds the admitted export bytes), compartment_projections
{comp: {sha256, records}}, evidence_root, dossier_root. The projection roots
are computed over the ID-FREE record documents (no publication_id/URLs) — so
altering parser/policy/projection/renderer inputs changes the namespace, and
the same inputs recompute the same namespace.

**Integrity manifest (sig.release-integrity/1):** publication_id +
descriptor_sha256 + artifacts[] {path, media_type, compartment, licence,
sha256, byte_size} + per-compartment completeness {record_count,
index_sha256} + input/output counts + completeness state. Its digest
`manifest_sha256` signs the release externally; nothing it covers embeds it.

**Mutable registry (outside the hash):** catalog.json (sig.publication/1
entries), latest.json (sig.latest-pointer/1), compat_index.json
(sig.compat-index/1 — as-of triple → publication), withdrawals.json
(sig.withdrawal-registry/1 — P32.5 DispositionRecord rows, public-safe
columns), activations/<pub>.json (sig.activation-record/1 — real UTC
timestamps live HERE, never in hashed bytes), staged/ (the public tree:
r/ + releases/ + entity/ overlay + conf/withdrawn_routes.conf).

**Withdrawal barrier before origin:** `sig-ops release-serve apply` walks the
staged tree against the CURRENT withdrawal registry via the P32.5 pure
`access_decision`/`latest_disposition` — denied routes get content-free
tombstone index.html (safe fields only: reason_category, authority, decided
date, policy version), denied artifact bytes are removed whole (immutable
artifacts denied, never rewritten), and `conf/withdrawn_routes.conf` emits
nginx `location =` exact-match `return 410` rules that match BEFORE the
`/r/` prefix location → before any file/CDN access.

## Acceptance criteria → test matrix

| # | AC | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | identical inputs → identical namespace + bytes; parser/policy/projection/renderer change → new namespace | `test_build_is_deterministic`, `test_descriptor_inputs_change_publication_id` |
| 2 | different bytes under an existing namespace refused | `test_reactivation_with_different_bytes_refused` |
| 3 | acyclic hash graph; final digest never inside hashed artifacts | `test_integrity_manifest_is_external_and_acyclic` |
| 4 | cited record beyond the 500-slice resolves exact released content offline/no-JS | `test_record_beyond_500_slice_resolves` + `test_record_html_has_no_scripts_and_links_latest_as_convenience` |
| 5 | invalid dates/rulesets never return unchanged "historical" page | `test_resolve_selector_variants`, `test_resolve_ambiguous_when_two_releases_share_the_triple` |
| 6 | incomplete compartment/index fails staging | `test_validate_and_activate_fail_on_missing_record`, `test_validate_fails_on_undeclared_artifact`, `test_validate_fails_on_index_digest_mismatch` |
| 7 | rollback + tombstone deterministic | `test_rollback_repoints_latest_and_overlay`, `test_rollback_refuses_unknown_release`, `test_rollback_to_a_withdrawn_release_is_refused`, `test_withdrawal_tombstones_deterministic`, `test_apply_is_deterministic` |
| 8 | withdrawal barrier before origin; withhold in R2 denies under R1 rollback | `test_withdrawal_denies_under_rollback`, `test_release_withdrawal_denies_the_whole_namespace`, `test_route_access_denies_routes_under_a_withdrawn_release`, `test_route_access_denies_record_carrying_a_denied_claim`, `test_apply_writes_tombstones_and_deny_map` (ops) |
| 9 | measured cost over full corpus | `test_measure_build_reports_cost` + `docs/build/reports/p32.13-release-generation.md` over `exports/out/national` (236,994 records) |
| 10 | compartment separation | licence per artifact asserted; claims sliced by own licence |

### Self-review findings → fixed in-run

- `route_access` (the serving check) missed **release-level** and
  **claim-level** denies (it checked only the route's own target) — now the
  namespace deny dominates and the staged claim index denies record routes
  carrying a denied claim; regression tests added.
- `rollback` to a wholly-withdrawn namespace crashed on the tombstoned index
  and would have repointed "latest" at a denied tree — now refused with
  `ReleaseError`; `_entity_overlay` skips tombstoned index paths.
- `peak_rss_kb` mis-labelled `ru_maxrss` (bytes on macOS) — schema field is
  now `peak_rss_bytes`, host-normalised.
- Digest-cycle: `manifest_sha256` removed from the landing artifact — the
  final digest stays external to the bytes it authenticates.
